title: latency-pattern-synthesis-midweek-watch-2026-06-21
content:
Shift window: 2026-06-20 23:00 - 2026-06-21 07:00 PST (APAC overlap)
Primary on-call: Maya Patel (this doc)
Secondary: Diego Morales
Handoff to next: Priya Kapoor at 07:00 PST

Summary (TL;DR):
- Observed repeated mid-latency spikes clustered between 01:10-02:05 and 04:30-05:05 UTC, impacting p95 for text-generation endpoints (hosted-api) and causing transient throttling on dedicated pools. No full outage; degraded tail latency and a small uptick in 5xxs (~0.4% baseline -> ~1.6% during spikes).
- Root cause not fully confirmed: hypothesis leans toward CPU contention on autoscaler control-plane jobs and prefix cache eviction storms correlated with a bursty user test job.
- Mitigations applied: temporary scale-up of dedicated pools, increased cache TTL for hot prefixes, and targeted routing to lower-latency replicas.

Timeline (concise):
- 23:05 PST: Pre-shift quick check; dashboards green.
- 00:58 PST (01:58 UTC): PagerDuty alert PD-12345 fired for p95 > 400ms on route /v1/generate for 3m window.
- 01:02 PST: Investigated; saw p95 spike to ~720ms, p50 stable. Error-rate up to 1.2%.
- 01:12 PST: Noted a sudden increase in autoscaler API latency (kube-controller pod metrics). Suspected control plane saturation. Opened SRE incident (SRE-987).
- 01:20 PST: Applied temporary scale-up: +2 nodes to dedicated pool alpha (manual override). Observed partial recovery by 01:32 PST.
- 01:40 PST: Detected repeated cache eviction events on prefix cache for model-rw-bert-13b. TTL miss rate increased ~8x.
- 02:05 PST: Tail latency returned near baseline after cache adjustments and node addition.
- 04:20 PST: Second, smaller spike detected; correlated with a large synthetic test job from partner-testing account (userID: partner-batch-19).
- 04:35 PST: Rate-limited partner-testing via temporary quota bump + blacklist for heavy batch path. Reduced burst; p95 normalized by 04:58 PST.
- 05:10 PST: Post-mortem triage call (ad-hoc) with infra and applied-ml to collect traces.

Diagnostics & Observations:
- Metrics: p95 peaked ~720-900ms; p99 saw smaller relative change (~1.2x). Token-CPU utilization on gpu-inference-nodes stayed <75%, but control-plane CPU (autoscaler/controller-manager) spiked to 95% for ~7-10m windows.
- Logs: repeated timeouts to ETCD and increased leader election churn around 01:10-01:25. Several GC pauses reported on the autoscaler pods (long-running Go STW noted).
- Traces: KV-cache eviction traces show many small prefixes being flushed then immediately re-requested -> thundering herd pattern.
- Recent deploys: serving-runtime PR #412 merged earlier that day contained a micro-optimization for kv cache invalidation. Possible regression in eviction heuristics.

Actions taken during shift:
- Manual scale-up of dedicated pool alpha (+2 nodes) to buy headroom (Maya).
- Increased prefix cache TTL for model-rw-bert-13b from 30s -> 90s (Diego).
- Throttled partner-testing job via quota rule; created temporary policy to limit concurrent batch requests (Priya).
- Re-routed a small percentage (5%) of traffic to eu-west region as an immediate fallback to reduce pressure on US cluster (Maya + infra ops).
- Opened SRE incident SRE-987 and linked to PD-12345; began evidence collection for post-incident review.

Runbook deviations / notes for runbook update:
- Current autorecovery guidance suggests auto-scale on replica CPU; does not cover control-plane autoscaler saturation. Add a new section: "Control-plane saturation indicators and emergency scale strategies".
- Add playbook entry for prefix cache eviction storms: detect by eviction-rate > 5/min and immediate step to increase TTL and enable hot-prefix sticky caching.
- Include a cross-team checklist for partner-scheduled synthetic jobs (product should notify SRE when partner runs large synthetic tests).

Outstanding/open follow-ups (owners + ETA):
- Post-incident deeper root cause analysis (trace correlation between GC pauses and leader churn) -> Owner: Jonah Reed -> ETA: 2026-06-25
- Revert/patch PR #412 if regression confirmed -> Owner: Diego Morales + infra -> ETA: 2026-06-22 (fast patch ready)
- Run a rolling restart of autoscaler pods with updated GC tuning flags; monitor leader election metrics -> Owner: Maya Patel -> ETA: 2026-06-22 (low-risk maintenance window)
- Add runbook sections (control-plane saturation + eviction storm steps) -> Owner: Priya Kapoor -> ETA: 2026-06-23 -> Target doc: Confluence latency-runbook update
- Partner engagement: notify partner-batch owner of rate-limits applied and request scheduled test windows -> Owner: Customer Success -> ETA: 2026-06-21 EOD

Post-shift checklist for next on-call (Priya / next):
- Verify autoscaler pods restarted and GC flags applied (kubectl top pods + prometheus query: kube_pod_container_resource_limits_cpu).
- Check leader-election metrics: etcd_request_duration_seconds and leader_changes_total for kube-controller-manager.
- Confirm TTL changes persisted for prefix cache and monitor eviction-rate over next 24h.
- Confirm PR #412 revert/patch status and coordinate canary if needed.
- Watch for partner test jobs; consider temporary quota change with scheduled windows.

Known risks / notes:
- If cache TTL is increased too aggressively it may increase memory usage on nodes; watch heap profile on runtime process.
- Autoscaler restarts may cause scaling flaps if applied without proper pod disruption budgets. Coordinate with infra before rolling restarts.

Slack links & references: #sre-watch thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SREW/watch-2026-06-21 (bookmark), incident thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SREW/pd-12345
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-987
Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/latency-runbook
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
PagerDuty: https://app.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-12345

Quick handoff notes (speakable):
- We had two latency spike windows tied to control-plane autoscaler saturation and a partner batch job. Temporary mitigations are in place (node scale up, cache TTL increase, partner throttling).
- Primary outstanding: confirm whether PR #412 changed eviction heuristics; if yes revert/patch asap.
- Next on-call: watch leader-election and eviction-rate dashboards; be prepared to coordinate a slow rolling restart of autoscaler/controller pods during a low-traffic window.

Appendix (commands & queries):
- p95 query example (Prometheus): sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le) -> histogram_quantile(0.95, ...)
- eviction rate: rate(prefix_cache_evictions_total[1m])
- pod CPU: kubectl top pods -n infra | grep autoscaler
- restart autoscaler (only with infra agreement): kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler -n infra

End of shift log.
